title: Throughput-per-watt rather than single-thread performance
decision: Target aggregate throughput and throughput per watt for commercial server workloads instead of maximizing single-thread performance.
alternatives_or_rejected: Conventional high-performance single-thread designs, such as wider or out-of-order cores, were treated as poor matches for the power envelope and workload mix.
rationale: Server workloads contain many parallel threads and are often limited by memory latency; many simple threads can use execution resources more efficiently within a fixed power budget.
outcome: The paper presents Niagara as a 32-thread processor intended to deliver high aggregate throughput at low power.

title: Eight simple cores instead of fewer complex cores
decision: Implement eight simple SPARC cores on a single die, with four threads per core, rather than a smaller number of complex cores.
alternatives_or_rejected: Fewer, more complex cores with out-of-order execution or wider issue were implicitly rejected because they consume more area and power and are less effective for high-thread-count server workloads.
rationale: Simple cores are smaller and lower power; available thread-level parallelism lets the chip spend its area and power budget on more threads rather than on single-thread sophistication.
outcome: The resulting chip has 8 cores and 32 hardware threads, trading per-thread speed for aggregate throughput.

title: Four-way fine-grained multithreading per core
decision: Each core supports four hardware threads and interleaves them fine-grained through a simple in-order pipeline.
alternatives_or_rejected: Single-threaded cores, coarse-grained multithreading, or adding out-of-order logic to hide latency were less attractive; the paper argues that fine-grained SMT hides latency more simply and with lower power.
rationale: Frequent thread switching keeps the pipeline busy during cache misses and long-latency operations without the complexity, area, and power cost of out-of-order execution.
outcome: The core achieves high utilization across threads while remaining simple and low power.

title: Memory hierarchy sized for many threads
decision: Use small private L1 caches per core and a shared on-chip L2 cache, with an integrated memory subsystem, to serve many simultaneous threads.
alternatives_or_rejected: Large private caches per core or relying primarily on off-chip memory would either consume too much area and power or provide insufficient bandwidth and latency for 32 threads.
rationale: Many threads generate high aggregate memory traffic; a shared L2 and integrated memory path reduce off-chip traffic and improve effective bandwidth within power limits.
outcome: The paper describes a memory system intended to sustain high throughput for multithreaded server workloads.

title: Architecture constrained by a low-power design point
decision: Keep the chip within a modest server power envelope by simplifying cores and relying on multithreading rather than raising frequency or adding complex single-thread features.
alternatives_or_rejected: High-frequency, high-power complex cores were rejected because power and cooling limits, and throughput-per-watt goals, dominate server economics.
rationale: Power is a first-order constraint; simpler cores plus many threads deliver better throughput per watt than pursuing single-thread speed.
outcome: The paper presents Niagara as achieving high throughput within a low-power design point.
